formulas.name: SUM
formulas.what: Adds numbers or whole ranges.
formulas.tip: Numbers stored as text are skipped without any warning. Compare COUNT with COUNTA to find them.

formulas.name: SUMIF
formulas.what: Adds the values that meet one condition.
formulas.tip: The sum range comes last here, but first in SUMIFS.

formulas.name: SUMIFS
formulas.what: Adds the values that meet several conditions at once.
formulas.tip: Every range must be the same size, or the formula returns #VALUE!.

formulas.name: COUNT
formulas.what: Counts the cells that contain numbers.
formulas.tip: Text that looks like a number is not counted.

formulas.name: COUNTA
formulas.what: Counts the cells that are not empty.
formulas.tip: A cell holding an empty text result ("") still counts as filled.

formulas.name: COUNTIF
formulas.what: Counts the cells that meet one condition.
formulas.tip: Put comparisons in quotes, for example ">100".

formulas.name: COUNTIFS
formulas.what: Counts the rows that meet several conditions.
formulas.tip: To compare with a cell, join the sign and the cell: ">"&H1.

formulas.name: AVERAGE
formulas.what: Returns the arithmetic mean.
formulas.tip: Empty cells are ignored but zeros are included, which changes the result.

formulas.name: AVERAGEIFS
formulas.what: Averages only the rows that meet your conditions.
formulas.tip: If nothing matches, the result is #DIV/0!.

formulas.name: MAX
formulas.what: Returns the largest value.
formulas.tip: Text and empty cells are ignored.

formulas.name: MIN
formulas.what: Returns the smallest value.
formulas.tip: A zero used as a placeholder will become the minimum.

formulas.name: MAXIFS
formulas.what: Returns the largest value among rows that meet your conditions.
formulas.tip: It returns 0, not an error, when nothing matches.

formulas.name: SUBTOTAL
formulas.what: Totals a list and ignores rows hidden by a filter. Function 9 means sum.
formulas.tip: Use 109 instead of 9 to also ignore rows you hid by hand.

formulas.name: SUMPRODUCT
formulas.what: Multiplies matching items and adds the results.
formulas.tip: The arrays must have the same number of rows and columns.

formulas.name: VLOOKUP
formulas.what: Finds a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from the same row.
formulas.tip: Leaving out FALSE gives an approximate match, which can return a wrong value without warning.

formulas.name: INDEX and MATCH
formulas.what: Looks up in any direction and works in every version.
formulas.tip: Keep both ranges the same height and use 0 for an exact match.

formulas.name: XLOOKUP
formulas.what: A modern lookup that can search left or right and shows your own message when nothing is found.
formulas.tip: It is not available in Excel 2019 or earlier. Use INDEX and MATCH for older versions.

formulas.name: IF
formulas.what: Chooses between two results.
formulas.tip: Put text results in quotes.

formulas.name: IFS
formulas.what: Checks conditions in order and returns the first that is true.
formulas.tip: End with TRUE as the catch-all, or unmatched rows show #N/A.

formulas.name: AND
formulas.what: True only when every condition is true.
formulas.tip: AND gives one answer for a whole range; it does not test row by row.

formulas.name: OR
formulas.what: True when at least one condition is true.
formulas.tip: Repeat the cell for each test: OR(A2="North",A2="East"), not OR(A2="North","East").

formulas.name: IFERROR
formulas.what: Shows your own result instead of an error.
formulas.tip: It hides every error, including broken references. For lookups, show a visible message instead of 0.

formulas.name: TRIM
formulas.what: Removes extra spaces, leaving single spaces between words.
formulas.tip: It does not remove non-breaking spaces copied from web pages.

formulas.name: PROPER
formulas.what: Capitalises the first letter of each word.
formulas.tip: Names such as McDonald need a manual check.

formulas.name: UPPER
formulas.what: Changes text to capital letters.
formulas.tip: Lookups already ignore capitals, so this is for display.

formulas.name: LEFT
formulas.what: Takes characters from the start of a text.
formulas.tip: The result is text, even when it looks like a number.

formulas.name: MID
formulas.what: Takes characters from the middle of a text.
formulas.tip: Positions start at 1, and spaces count.

formulas.name: LEN
formulas.what: Counts the characters in a cell.
formulas.tip: Compare with LEN of the untrimmed cell to find hidden spaces.

formulas.name: SUBSTITUTE
formulas.what: Replaces one piece of text with another.
formulas.tip: It is case-sensitive.

formulas.name: TEXTJOIN
formulas.what: Joins many cells with a separator.
formulas.tip: Set the second argument to TRUE to skip empty cells.

formulas.name: TEXT
formulas.what: Turns a number or date into text in a chosen format.
formulas.tip: The result is text and cannot be summed. Format codes can differ with regional settings.

formulas.name: EOMONTH
formulas.what: Returns the last day of a month, before or after a date.
formulas.tip: Format the result cell as a date, or you will see a serial number.

formulas.name: NETWORKDAYS
formulas.what: Counts Monday to Friday between two dates, including both ends.
formulas.tip: For Friday and Saturday or Sunday-only weekends, use NETWORKDAYS.INTL.

formulas.name: DATEDIF
formulas.what: Counts complete years or months between two dates.
formulas.tip: Excel does not suggest it as you type. Microsoft advises against the "MD" unit.

formulas.name: WEEKDAY
formulas.what: Returns the day of the week as a number. With type 2, Monday is 1.
formulas.tip: Without the second argument, Sunday is 1.

formulas.name: Target achievement %
formulas.what: Shows how much of a target has been reached.
formulas.tip: For a team, divide total actual by total target. Do not average each person's percentage.

formulas.name: Growth %
formulas.what: Measures change from one period to the next.
formulas.tip: If the old value is zero or negative, the percentage has no useful meaning.

formulas.name: Weighted average
formulas.what: Averages values where some count more than others. Here, the average selling price per unit.
formulas.tip: A simple average of prices ignores how many units were sold at each price.

formulas.name: Running total
formulas.what: Adds up values as you go down a list. The example is the total after six rows.
formulas.tip: Lock only the starting cell with $ so the end moves as you copy.

formulas.name: RANK
formulas.what: Shows the position of a number in a list.
formulas.tip: Lock the list with $. Equal values get the same rank.

formulas.name: LARGE
formulas.what: Returns the k-th largest value.
formulas.tip: k cannot be larger than the number of values.

formulas.name: ROUND
formulas.what: Rounds to a chosen number of decimal places. Negative places round to tens, hundreds or thousands.
formulas.tip: Formatting hides decimals but keeps them. ROUND changes the stored value.

formulas.name: FILTER
formulas.what: Returns the rows that meet a condition. Here the results are added up.
formulas.tip: It needs empty cells below and beside it, or it shows #SPILL!.

formulas.name: UNIQUE
formulas.what: Lists each value once. Here the unique regions are counted.
formulas.tip: Extra spaces make two entries look different. Clean the data first.
